newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars surge as bonds rally on election.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars surge as bonds rally on election.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's re-election and the prospect of a continued Republican majority in Congress propelled SIMEX Eurodollar futures higher as U.S. bonds surged in Tokyo on Wednesday.
"The whole picture looks pretty good with the Republicans gaining a foothold in the Senate and Clinton coming back," said a dealer with an Asian institution.

He said the bullish mood was unlikely to be dampened by a 10-year note auction later on Wednesday as the market would continue to get a "psychological lift" from the election results during the U.S. session.
The most active March Eurodollar contract finished at 94.47 against its IMM close at 94.46 after hitting a high of 94.50.
A Japanese bank dealer said it was likely to head towards 94.52/55, with support seen at 94.40.
The U.S. bond market rally did not extend itself to Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, which fell sharply as the market underwent a correction after recent sharp gains.
"After the U.S. election results, Tokyo players started taking profit on cash JGBs," said the Japanese bank dealer.

"There was a flight to quality from JGBs to T-bonds," said the trader at the Asian institution, adding that the Nikkei's hefty gains and close above the key 21,000 level had also pulled down JGB and Euroyen futures.
"When the JGBs broke below 126.00, there was a lot of nervousness and people were scurrying to cover their long positions," he said.
"But the JGBs' (recent) move has been unwarranted and this could pave the way for further down moves," he said, adding that December JGBs would find some support at 125.50 and 125.35.
They settled at 125.76 against their previous 126.37.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.22 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.28. It hit a low of 99.21 and saw a healthy turnover of 25,093 lots.
